title: Choose the atlas composition
question: Three ways to explore the same source-backed concepts, within the Dyne theme. Choose the arrangement you want to read and return to.

options.label: Junction atlas
options.thesis: Choose an idea, then follow one named connection at a time.
options.viewport: Starting concepts lead into a large still junction: Human dignity, grounds, Human rights; full reasoning follows below.
options.risk: The active neighborhood is clear, but distant relationships require returning to the overview.

options.label: Atlas beside the reader
options.thesis: Keep the concept neighborhood beside the reasoning as you explore.
options.viewport: Desktop places the map next to a full reader; phones open the reader full width with a compact map and named connections.
options.risk: The map needs a restrained phone layout so it does not crowd the reading.

options.label: Question regions
options.thesis: Enter the atlas through a human question, then explore the ideas behind it.
options.viewport: Questions such as What makes a person worthy? organize the overview; Human dignity opens its connected neighborhood and full reader.
options.risk: The editorial groups can feel like extra navigation unless concepts remain directly available.
